title: 1960'S DOLLS HOUSE WITH VARIOU...
reason: Large homemade 1960s style dolls house with a tub of handmade-looking furniture; no maker marks, about $60 to $150.
findings: Five photos (front closed, side, doors open, interior close-up, and a tub of loose contents). Homemade-looking painted board or timber dolls house (title: W-96 cm), cream with a green gabled roof and a two-door front opening to a two-storey, six-room interior with wallpapers, carpet squares, a staircase, a hanging cat picture and ornaments, and fabric curtains at the windows and inside the doors. The tub holds Ziploc bags marked CH in pen with small wooden furniture (a spindle cot with blue bedding, a loom or spinning-wheel type piece, chairs, a long bench with a floral cushion), a few small dolls (one in a red hooded outfit), fabric bedding, a fleece-type rug and a metal tray. The small patches on the front gable and side, enlarged, are torn paper or paint residue, not writing. No maker's label or stamp anywhere (only Ziploc branding and lot tickets), so it looks homemade rather than Tri-ang or Lundby. The 1960s date is plausible from the wallpapers but cannot be confirmed.
condition: Paint is scuffed and chipped in places, with small torn paper and paint marks on the gable and right side. Hinges, interior papers, carpets and curtains look intact. Furniture is loose in bags and not itemised, so completeness and condition of the miniatures are unknown.
rescore_note: Large homemade painted dolls house (96 cm wide) with six papered and carpeted rooms, curtains and a tub of unitemised furniture and small dolls; no maker (not Tri-ang or Lundby), scuffed paint, bulky, and the condition of the miniatures is unknown, so appeal is mainly to families, low-mid band.
